question: A man sells a cupboard at a certain price S, get 20% of the profit on his selling price. If the price at which he buys the cupboard increases by 10% and he sells it at a. 4% higher price than S, then his profit percentage will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial Selling Price (SP) = 100.

Profit is 20% on SP ⇒ Profit = 20 ⇒ Initial Cost Price (CP) = 100 − 20 = 80.

New CP increases by 10% ⇒ New CP = 80 + 8 = 88.

New SP increases by 4% ⇒ New SP = 100 + 4 = 104.

New Profit = 104 − 88 = 16 ⇒ Profit % = (16 ÷ 88) × 100 = 18.18%.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP) = S

Initial Profit = 20% of the Selling Price

New Cost Price (CP) is 10% more than the initial CP.

New Selling Price (SP) is 4% more than the initial SP.

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price = Selling Price − Profit

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100
